cases.sentence: ___ был верен, и зависть Степана Аркадьевича была приятна Левину.
cases.translation: The count was correct, and Stepan Arkadyich's envy was pleasant to Levin.
cases.explain: «Счёт» is the subject of «был верен», so it stands in the Nominative case.

cases.sentence: Весловский вспоминал с наслаждением свои похождения у ___, угостившего его водкой.
cases.translation: Veslovsky recalled with delight his adventures with the peasant who had treated him to vodka.
cases.explain: The preposition «у» governs the Genitive case: «у мужика».

cases.sentence: Счет был верен, и зависть Степана Аркадьевича была приятна ___.
cases.translation: The count was correct, and Stepan Arkadyich's envy was pleasant to Levin.
cases.explain: «Левину» is the experiencer with «приятна» ("pleasant to someone"), hence Dative.
The preposition «на» expressing motion to a place governs the Accusative case: «на квартиру».

cases.sentence: он стал смеяться над своим голодным ___.
cases.translation: He began to laugh at his own hungry irritation.
cases.explain: The preposition «над» governs the Instrumental case: «над озлоблением».

cases.sentence: из всей провизии, отпущенной Ките в таком ___, что казалось, нельзя было ее доесть в неделю.
cases.translation: of all the provisions given to Kitty in such abundance that it seemed impossible to finish in a week.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» (location/manner) governs the Prepositional case: «в изобилии».

reading.ru: Охотничья примета, что если не упущен первый зверь и первая птица, то поле будет счастливо, оказалось справедливою.
reading.question: What hunting omen proved true for Levin?
options: That if the first beast and first bird are not missed, the whole hunt will be lucky
That hunting in the rain brings bad luck
That a hunter who talks too much scares away the game
That the best hunting is always at sunset
reading.correct: That if the first beast and first bird are not missed, the whole hunt will be lucky
reading.explain: The passage states the hunting omen — that if the first beast and bird are not missed, the day's hunt will be lucky — proved true.

reading.ru: Товарищи его уж давно проснулись и успели проголодаться и позавтракать.
reading.question: What had Levin's companions already done by the time he returned?
options: They had woken up long before, gotten hungry, and had breakfast
They had gone out searching for him
They had packed up and left
They had gone back to sleep
reading.correct: They had woken up long before, gotten hungry, and had breakfast
reading.explain: The text says his companions had long since woken up and managed to get hungry and have breakfast.

reading.ru: Счет был верен, и зависть Степана Аркадьевича была приятна Левину.
reading.question: How did Levin feel about Stepan Arkadyich's reaction to the game count?
options: He found Stepan Arkadyich's envy pleasant
He was embarrassed by Stepan Arkadyich's envy
He felt guilty for outhunting his friend
reading.correct: He found Stepan Arkadyich's envy pleasant
reading.explain: The text says the count was correct, and Stepan Arkadyich's envy was pleasant to Levin.

reading.ru: У меня новый телохранитель, Марья Власьевна.
reading.question: Who did Kitty mention as her new "bodyguard" in her note?
reading.explain: In her note Kitty writes that she has a new bodyguard, Marya Vlasyevna, who was the midwife.

reading.ru: Одна состояла в том, что рыжая пристежная, очевидно переработавшая вчера, не ела корма и была скучна.
reading.question: What was the first of the two small troubles Levin faced?
options: The chestnut trace-horse, apparently overworked the day before, was off her feed and listless
One of the dogs had gone missing
A wheel on the carriage had broken
The gun had jammed during the hunt
reading.correct: The chestnut trace-horse, apparently overworked the day before, was off her feed and listless
reading.explain: The text says one trouble was that the chestnut trace-horse, having evidently overworked the day before, would not eat and was listless.

reading.ru: Оказалось, что не только пирожков, но и цыплят уже не было.
reading.question: What did Levin discover about the food when he got back hungry from the hunt?
options: There were neither pirozhki nor chickens left
There was plenty of food left over
The cook had prepared a new feast
reading.correct: There were neither pirozhki nor chickens left
reading.explain: It turned out that not only were there no pirozhki left, but no chicken either.

reading.ru: Говядину скушали, я кость собакам отдал
reading.question: What did Filipp say had happened to the beef?
options: It had been eaten, and he had given the bone to the dogs
It had spoiled and been thrown out
Vasenka had taken it with him
reading.correct: It had been eaten, and he had given the bone to the dogs
reading.explain: Filipp answers that the beef was eaten and he gave the bone to the dogs.

reading.question: What especially amused Veslovsky on the way home?
options: A peasant's advice not to covet others' wives but to get one of his own
A joke Stepan Arkadyich told about hunting
The sight of the tired horses
Levin's outburst about the missing food
reading.correct: A peasant's advice not to covet others' wives but to get one of his own
reading.explain: Veslovsky recalled the peasant's words telling him not to covet others' wives but to seek his own, and these words especially amused him.
